segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest for October 29, 2026.
We've got 18 stories today, including updates on physical AI valuations, rising North American robot orders, and new funding for physical AI training.
From Humanoids Daily, Physical Intelligence Reportedly Seeks $1B at a $20B Valuation.
This report details the company's current fundraising goal and valuation.
Physical Intelligence is reportedly seeking at least one billion dollars in funding based on an estimated valuation of twenty billion dollars.
The company is currently opening its models to external developers through an API beta designed to facilitate robot model training and inference.
Existing investors Avenir and Lux Capital are reportedly in discussions to lead this potential financing round.

The company's objective is to establish a shared intelligence layer capable of learning across diverse robot bodies and applications, aiming to make research accessible for real-world application development.
This development signals a push toward unified, multi-body artificial intelligence systems.
The industry should monitor the progress of this financing and the subsequent development of the shared intelligence framework.
From The Robot Report, North American robot orders climb 24.8% in Q3 of 2026, says A3.
This report details the growth trajectory of robot orders across North America during the third quarter of 2026, revealing a significant increase in both unit volume and monetary value.

The growth was fueled by positive returns observed in automotive original equipment manufacturer orders alongside substantial increases in demand across diverse sectors including semiconductors, life sciences, and plastics.
Collaborative robots specifically experienced a notable fifty-six percent increase in unit volume during this same period.
This positive market momentum occurred despite earlier decreases noted in the first half of 2026 for certain market segments.
This trend indicates an increasing diversification of robot adoption across various industrial applications.
The data suggests continued broad-based expansion within the advanced manufacturing and technology sectors.

From Robotics & Automation News, Maxinsights raises thirty million dollars to build a training data platform for physical artificial intelligence, expanding its system for generating real-world activity data for robot and AI training.

The company has successfully collected over two million hours of human activity, with one point five million of those hours being made ready for model training, ensuring exposure to real-world variations.
To achieve this, Maxinsights developed tools such as MaxLoop for monitoring footage quality and MaxGlove for capturing tactile information like grip force.

This collected data is critical for training models such as Genesis AI, which utilized this information for its GENE-26.5 model, underscoring the necessity of capturing real-world data, including edge cases, for effective robot deployment.
This development indicates a growing industry focus on high-fidelity physical data collection for advancing autonomous systems.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control".
This story explores the integration of industrial artificial intelligence with human control mechanisms to achieve adaptive operational models.

Living digital twins combine high-fidelity operational data with control systems to mirror industrial plant dynamism, and artificial intelligence is central to evolving these twins into adaptive, living models capable of intervening in the physical world.
Agentic AI facilitates systems acting autonomously within defined parameters, requiring robust data synchronization from IoT sensors and predictive models to maintain a connected operational record.
This integration across the value chain is projected to yield increased resilience and sustainable industrial operation.
The industry focus should remain on developing secure and synchronized systems for autonomous industrial control.
From MIT News - Robotics, "A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine".
This report details the development of a robotic enteroscope inspired by snakes designed to navigate the small intestine for enhanced diagnosis and treatment.
The system utilizes multifunctional actuators and textured coatings to move through narrow passages by mimicking snake locomotion.
It is equipped with instruments for imaging, drug delivery, and taking biopsies of polyps, and external controllers guide the robot through the intestine.
Animal studies confirmed the robot's capacity to travel several feet while successfully performing these interventions.
This advancement suggests potential applications for minimally invasive medical procedures and further development in soft robotics technology.
From Humanoids Daily, Audi tests Agile Robots’ mobile humanoids for automotive parts sequencing, a project focused on optimizing material handling operations.

The testing involves utilizing mobile humanoid robots to sequence automotive parts by picking components from containers and arranging them for assembly, targeting a material-supply operation scale of one million picks daily.
The system employs dual-arm manipulation and a mobile base to manage varied, unsorted components within logistics environments.

Virtual testing, supported by a digital twin developed with NVIDIA Omniverse and Dassault Systèmes, is currently assessing the feasibility of the proposed sequencing methodology prior to physical deployment.
Successful deployment hinges upon consistent physical performance metrics such as pick rates and operating costs.
This development indicates progress in applying advanced mobile robotics to complex industrial logistics tasks.
Future developments will focus on scaling the operational efficiency of such systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, Neura Robotics and TUM open €17 million RoboGym and unveil new humanoid.
This report details the establishment of a robotics center and the introduction of a new humanoid robot.
Neura Robotics and the Technical University of Munich have opened a robotics center near Munich Airport with an investment of seventeen million euros.
This facility incorporates the TUM RoboGym, a space exceeding two thousand three hundred square meters designed for robotics research, training, and industrial applications.
The center facilitates training for companies across ten industries to teach robots real-world tasks such as material handling and loading.
Additionally, Neura Robotics introduced its latest humanoid robot, the 4NE1 Gen 4, which utilizes Neuron AI and is engineered for series production.
This collaboration seeks to advance physical artificial intelligence and build an international network of training resources.
The developments indicate a push toward practical physical AI implementation across various sectors.
From Humanoids Daily, AGIBOT introduced Worken, new AI models, and the G2 Max at Innovation Day 2026, detailing advancements in robotics and artificial intelligence.

The presentation focused on the introduction of Worken, a framework defined by the formula Worken equals Active Robots multiplied by Autonomous Working Hours multiplied by the Output Efficiency Ratio, alongside new hardware and software.
AGIBOT unveiled the AHA3 hardware, which integrates locomotion, interaction, and task execution.
Furthermore, new AI models were presented, including the GO-3 Preview for reasoning and action, and the WITA-Omni 1.0 for human-robot interaction.
The G2 Max robot was introduced, designed for industrial handling with a four-hundred kilogram dual-arm capacity and a working height range of zero point one to two point five meters.
Link-U OS 1.0 was also announced as an open-source operating system with a plan for full open-sourcing by the close of 2026.
This development signals further integration of measurable productivity metrics and advanced multimodal AI capabilities in robotic systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing"
reports on Faraday Future's strategy to establish a United States robotics business through localization of production.
The company plans to establish a US robot factory by the end of 2026, with the first US-assembled robot anticipated in February 2027.
The transition focuses on localizing production to improve regulatory compliance, enhance supply chain resilience, and ensure quality control, rather than simply relocating assembly lines.
This initiative involves leveraging existing electric vehicle manufacturing infrastructure to create synergies with robotics development.

Faraday Future views vehicles and robotics as interconnected components within a broader physical AI ecosystem, sharing foundational technologies such as artificial intelligence, perception, and computing.
Success is defined by building a sustainable US-based physical AI and robotics ecosystem through manufacturing capacity and product launches.
This movement indicates a focus on domestic supply chain integration within the advanced technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Xpeng Iron batteries enter small batch output ahead of robot".
This report details the commencement of small batch production for the batteries intended for the Xpeng Iron robot.
Xpeng announced a dedicated solid-state battery design specifically engineered for the robot's restricted space, incorporating safety features such as impact resistance.
Reports indicate the battery chemistry remains a point of ambiguity, with some sources suggesting the use of a solid liquid hybrid or semi-solid state rather than an entirely solid-state design.
Xpeng has set a target for mass production of the Iron robot by the end of 2026, with initial deployment planned for roles such as in-store assistance.
This development indicates ongoing progress in integrating advanced power solutions into autonomous robotics.
Industry focus will remain on the timeline for full robot production and battery scalability.
From Humanoids Daily, "Robbyant’s Embodied AI Challenge Will Send 15 Teams to a Real-Robot Final in Shanghai".
This report details the upcoming Embodied AI Challenge where fifteen teams will compete in a final stage using physical robots.
The event is a forty-eight-hour hackathon focused on adapting artificial intelligence models to physical robotic systems.
Competitors will utilize AgileX Robotics’ Cobot Magic platform to accomplish the objective, which is based on the LingBot-VLA 2.0 model.
Initially, over one thousand eight hundred teams registered for the challenge.
The event seeks to evaluate the efficacy of vision-language-action models when applied to tangible hardware.
Final specifications regarding scoring and robot access are presently under finalization.
This competition signifies a focus on practical application and physical embodiment within the development of advanced AI systems.
Industry observers will monitor the final outcomes of this challenge.
From Humanoids Daily, Unitree’s Quarterly Revenue Surges 70% as R&D Spending Weighs on Profit.
This report details the financial performance of Unitree for the third quarter, noting a substantial increase in revenue concurrent with significant investment in research and development.

The company recorded third-quarter revenue of 665 million yuan, representing a seventy percent increase, while net profit attributable to shareholders declined by seventeen point four percent to 112.7 million yuan.

Research and development spending escalated by two hundred forty-nine point six percent, reaching 127 million yuan, with this increased expenditure directed toward embodied-intelligence models and computing capacity.
Despite the strong sales growth, the net profit did not align with the revenue expansion.
This trend indicates a period of aggressive technological investment within the robotics sector.
From The Robot Report, "Warp Sciences emerges from stealth, to apply robotics to drug research".
This report details the recent fundraising and operational plans of Warp Sciences to leverage robotics and artificial intelligence in drug discovery.
The company successfully raised two hundred fifteen million dollars to establish chemistry infrastructure utilizing robotics and AI for accelerating the process of finding new pharmaceuticals.
Warp Sciences is developing a United States-based contract research organization designed to integrate chemists, robotics, and artificial intelligence for molecule development and testing.

The company intends to generate real-world data to train artificial intelligence, thereby enabling laboratories to test a greater number of hypotheses with increased efficiency through methods like lead optimization analog synthesis for rapid molecular comparison.
The organization focuses on establishing a sovereign biotechnology partner to secure speed, quality, and intellectual property protection domestically.
This development signals a push toward integrating advanced robotics and machine learning into the core of pharmaceutical research.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, TORCH HAND 2!".
This segment reports on the specifications and initial assessment of the TORCH HAND 2 robotic hand, which scored a six out of ten on the Humanoid.Guide Hand Score.

The TORCH HAND 2, manufactured by TorchKernel Robotics, measures two hundred millimeters by one hundred five millimeters by fifty millimeters and weighs zero point four eight kilograms, with a retail price of six thousand five hundred US dollars.
The evaluation indicates that the hand achieved a four out of five rating for degrees of freedom, demonstrating high dexterity, while it received a two out of five rating for strength.
This balance suggests the design prioritizes dexterity over gripping power.
Production of this robotic hand is currently underway for commercial availability in robotic systems.
The release of this device signals further development in the practical application of dexterous manipulation in robotics.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, NE01!".
This report details the specifications and current capabilities of the NE01 humanoid robot developed by GENISOM AI, highlighting its limited functional demonstration.
The robot measures one hundred forty-five centimeters in height and weighs forty kilograms, constructed from an aluminum alloy structure with integrated joint modules.
It possesses the mechanical capacity to move at ten kilometers per hour and generate up to one hundred eighty newton meters of torque.
Verified capabilities include obstacle avoidance and the sorting of goods, although navigation and manipulation skills have been rated very low, scoring one out of five.
Despite design intent for mass production, the NE01 is presently regarded as a preliminary platform with demonstrated, limited functionality.
This development indicates ongoing research into the practical application and refinement of humanoid robotics.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, CYBORG H02!".
This segment details the introduction of the CYBORG H02, a robotic hand from Cyborg Robotics, which has received a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of 7 out of 10.
The device is a robotic hand featuring five fingers and a tendon mechanism modeled after the human hand, weighing 750 grams and measuring 248 by 114 by 52 millimeters.
Six electric motors control the tendon architecture, which dictates the hand's actuation and joint design.
The system was evaluated with a Strength rating of four out of five and a Degrees of Freedom rating of three out of five.
The product is currently listed as in production with an advertised price of four thousand US dollars.
This development signals further advancement in dexterous robotic manipulation capabilities within the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Mornine!".
This segment reports on the development and commercial deployment of Mornine, a full-size bipedal humanoid robot.
The machine measures one hundred sixty-seven centimeters tall and weighs seventy kilograms, representing a new advancement in commercial robotics.
The robot is constructed with an aluminum alloy structure and is equipped with electric joint actuators.
Development was undertaken by AiMOGA, a subsidiary of the Chery Group.
Mornine possesses a maximum speed of three point six kilometers per hour and has demonstrated the capability to sort goods and avoid obstacles, possessing a strength capacity of three kilograms.
Production of this unit is currently taking place in China, with a listed price of approximately forty-one thousand four hundred US dollars.
The ongoing production signals increased commercial viability for advanced humanoid robotics in industrial settings.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, W-Bot!".
This segment details the introduction of a wheeled humanoid robot designed for manipulation in confined spaces.
The robot features a compact base and an articulated upper body facilitating work in restricted environments.
The device stands at one hundred seventy-eight centimeters tall and utilizes folding joints to achieve a reach of two point two meters.
Its arms possess forty-three degrees of freedom, with each arm capable of lifting ten kilograms.
The robot is outfitted with onboard computing, depth cameras, LiDAR, and force sensors to enhance environmental awareness and interaction.
Primary functions include sorting goods and assembling products within constrained work areas.
This technology points toward advancements in dexterous manipulation within complex industrial settings.
And that’s all for today's firmware update!
Hope your algorithms are running smoothly.
Go forth and code brilliantly, and until tomorrow, keep those circuits buzzing.
See you next time!
